Toyota Surges Post Q2 Earnings: Is the Stock Worth Buying Now?
sum: Toyota TM shares rose more than 9% yesterday following its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results, taking its monthly gains to roughly 20%, outperforming the industry and its peers Honda HMC and Nissan NSANY. While Honda shares gained 14.5% over the past month, Nissan stock fell roughly 2%.

The rally may appear surprising at first glance, considering the automaker reported an 18.5% year-over-year decline in net income to ¥759.4 billion in second-quarter fiscal 2027. However, investors focused on two more encouraging developments — a stronger full-year profit outlook and an expanded shareholder-return program.

Toyota's latest results suggest that its operating business is performing better than its bottom line indicates. Meanwhile, its hybrid-focused strategy, improving North American profitability and higher shareholder payouts offer reasons for optimism. But with the stock having rallied sharply, is TM still worth buying? Let's dig deeper.
Toyota Motor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Toyota Motor Corporation Quote

The decline in net income does not fully capture the improvement in Toyota's operations. The decline came from foreign-exchange losses and higher finance costs, which together outweighed an improvement in operating profit. Operating income grew 34% during the quarter under review.

The automotive division, Toyota's core, saw revenues rise 8.2% to ¥11.96 trillion. Its operating profit jumped 53% to ¥878.2 billion, helped by favorable currency movements, pricing actions and lower expenses, though higher material costs took a bite. The smaller "All Other" businesses also did well, with revenues up 19.6% and operating profit up 51% to ¥47.3 billion.
Financial services was the soft spot. Revenues rose 14% to ¥1.36 trillion, but operating income fell 13.8% to ¥196.7 billion. It is a modest drag next to the strength in autos.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Begins Rebound as U.S. Stock Gains and Oil Price Plunge Offer Support, but AI and Semiconductor Shares Weigh
sum: The Nikkei 225 began trading higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on November 5, opening at 62,384.73 yen, up 196.10 yen (0.32%) from the previous trading day. Buying led the market, carrying over the momentum from gains in all three major U.S. stock indexes the prior day.

Two factors pushed the market up. One was the firm performance of the U.S. stock market as it digested the results of the U.S. midterm elections. The other was a sharp drop in crude oil prices as views spread that tensions in the Middle East were easing. Lower energy costs support investor sentiment through both corporate earnings and household burdens.
Among blue-chip shares, Toyota Motor (7203.T) surged, while Sony Group (6758.T) and index-heavyweight Fast Retailing (9983.T) were quoted higher.

On the other hand, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor-related shares saw notable declines. SoftBank Group (9984.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), and Advantest (6857.T) all fell sharply, as caution over the direction of AI regulation continued to simmer.

In the previous day's trading on November 4, these three semiconductor and AI-related stocks alone pushed the Nikkei 225 down by about 1,241 yen at one point. Selling tends to concentrate in stocks with large index weightings, and this structure continues to amplify swings across the broader market.

Among market participants, the near-term focus is whether buybacks will emerge in the sharply fallen semiconductor shares. On the previous day, some stocks such as Fast Retailing and Nintendo (7974.T) rose, so the market was not uniformly lower. Some see the fact that buying interest is not one-sided as a sign of the market's underlying resilience.

On the overseas front, reports on vote counting in the U.S. midterm elections were also coming in during Tokyo trading hours, and market participants are focused on how U.S. long-term interest rates and foreign exchange rates react. Domestically, earnings announcements from companies such as IHI (7013.T), Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T), and NTT (9432.T) are scheduled during trading hours, and stock price reactions to individual earnings results could divide winners and losers within sectors.

The only U.S. pure-play humanoid robotics stock begins trading this week
sum: Shareholders of Churchill Capital Corp XI CCXI approved the business combination with Agility Robotics, a leading humanoid robotics and physical AI company. Agility's gross capital raise in connection with the proposed business combination and related financings is expected to be approximately $465M, before transaction expenses. The gross capital raise includes approximately $164M from Churchill XI’s trust account, approximately $201M from a common stock PIPE committed at $10 per share, led by Foxconn FXCOF with participation from leading existing and new institutional investors, and $100M of equity funding already received.

Agility Robotics is expected to enter the public markets well capitalized to execute its planned investments in commercial expansion and support growing customer demand. Notably, Agility said it will be the only U.S. publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with proven, active commercial deployments. Trading is expected to start on November 5.

Agility Robotics emerged from Oregon State University’s Dynamic Robotics Laboratory in 2015, founded by Jonathan Hurst, Damion Shelton, and Mikhail Jones. An early two-legged research robot, Cassie, launched in 2017 and provided the foundation for Digit, introduced in 2019 with a torso, arms, sensors, and greater computing capacity. The company progressively shifted from locomotion research toward practical material-handling jobs in warehouses and factories. Former Microsoft executive MSFT and Magic Leap CEO Peggy Johnson became Agility’s CEO in 2024 to lead commercialization and scaling. "Humanoid robotics is moving from what’s possible to what’s practical, and our focus is on building the technology, customer relationships, and operating foundation required to deploy it at scale," stated Johnson earlier this month.

Commercial milestones include a 2024 robots-as-a-service agreement with GXO Logistics GXO, allowing customers to obtain robot services rather than buy the hardware outright. Agility has recently reported commercial deployments involving GXO GXO, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada TM, and MercadoLibre MELI, alongside deployment commitments across nine customer facilities.

Ford’s 20% Sales Forecasts Meets A 38% Stock Collapse
sum: Jim Farley keeps pitching bold growth targets for Ford while Wall Street responds by punishing the stock harder than almost any major automaker. Something in his vision and the reality of the market is not adding up.

Ford (NASDAQ: F | F Price Prediction) CEO Jim Farley has been extremely optimistic about the No. 2 US car company’s prospects. Recently, he said Ford’s Fathom EV pickup would sell 100,000 units in its first year of production. That ignored stiffening competition as legacy car companies, beaten back by poor sales, have slowly reentered the US market, which he also abandoned. Add Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to the mix. US EV sales are down 30% in the first nine months of this year. Car sales in the US are generally flat. The average age of a car on the road in the US is 12 years. The average new car price is $51,000.

Farley told many of his workers that his goal was to raise Ford’s unit sales by 20% by 2032. The WSJ reported, “The company’s global strategy turns on Farley’s emphasis on no longer making “boring” vehicles, which for now has left it without the budget-friendly small sedans and SUVs it used to give priority to.” However, other car companies are likely to abandon their “boring” models as well.
Wall St. has had enough of Ford’s sales and forecast, driving the stock down 38% in the last five years. The S&P is up 61% over the same period.

It is hard to say how Farley will reach his target. His market share in the US ranks third. Ahead are the world’s largest car company, Toyota (NYSE: TM), and Detroit crosstown rival GM (NYSE: GM). And Ford’s sales in the US are falling. It has far from modest sales in China and the EU. It is stuck in America.

As has been said over and over again, Ford is a big SUV and pickup company, which has served it very well in its home market. Americans continue to buy cars with relatively low mileage, but it’s hard to say whether that will continue with high gas prices.

Farley has also said a good deal about his anxiety if Chinese EVs move into the US market. If they build those cars here, these EVs may have a chance to sell in America. Car companies beyond Ford would have significant sales problems as well.

News / Used-import sales jump 18.4%
sum: The number of used-imported cars registered in New Zealand totalled 8,285 last month, an increase of 18.4 per cent from 6,999 units in October 2025.
Year-to-date, there have been 76,774 registrations, which is 7.5 per cent higher than 71,441 units at the same stage a year ago.
Toyota’s Aqua was the best-selling model in October with 900 registrations – up by 16.4 per cent from 773 units in the same month last year – and a market share of 10.9 per cent.

The top four models were unchanged from September, with the Toyota Prius next on 518 units and 6.3 per cent of the market, Nissan’s Note scoring 465 sales and 5.6 per cent, and Toyota’s Corolla on 429 and 5.5 per cent.
Nissan’s Leaf, pictured, completed the top five with 262 units and a 3.2 per cent market shares after its sales jumped 138.2 per cent from 110 in October last year.

The Aqua, pictured, leads the year-to-date standings on 7,547 units and a market share of 9.8 per cent, followed by the Prius with 4,709 and 6.1 per cent. The Note is third on 3,910 units and 5.1 per cent.
Toyota was the leading marque in October with 3,249 registrations for 39.2 per cent of the market. Its monthly total was up by 21.1 per cent from 2,684 in the same month of 2025.

RS Garage Shares its Toyota 2JZ Build Recipe
sum: The Toyota 2JZ has earned a reputation as one of the import performance world’s most durable foundations, but Jay Meagher of RS Garage sees its appeal as something more than simply an engine capable of surviving four-digit horsepower.

To Meagher, the 2JZ is almost the Japanese equivalent of the small block Chevy – a well-engineered, versatile platform that responds to relatively straightforward modifications and can deliver impressive power without requiring the builder to reinvent the entire engine.

“You can take a stock one, tune it properly if it’s a turbo 2JZ engine, and you can make seven or 800 horsepower for a large block of time,” Meagher says. “From there, if you want to go up a level, you can put pistons and rods in one, some valve springs, some camshafts, and you’ve got a really good 1,000-horsepower engine.”

For this particular Engine of the Week build, however, Meagher took the combination a step further. The RS Garage 2JZ uses a 94mm-stroke Brian Crower crankshaft, Brian Crower titanium connecting rods and custom-spec CP pistons. Combined with the engine’s variable intake cam, the stroker rotating assembly is intended to produce the kind of broad powerband Meagher considers ideal for a 1,000-1,200-horsepower street car.
That distinction matters. Jay has experience with 2JZ combinations producing considerably more horsepower, but he doesn’t necessarily consider a bigger number to be a better street engine.
“I think the best use for the engine is in that 1,000-1,200 horsepower range because you can build a nice engine that lives,” he says.

The engine’s 94mm stroke is a significant departure from the factory 86mm dimension, and Meagher recommends the stroker approach for many street-oriented customers because of what the additional displacement does for turbo response and drivability.

GAC Group Soars 14% on Trading Resumption, Plans A-Share Issuance to Acquire Half of FAW Toyota
sum: GAC Group (02238.HK) saw its shares surge after trading resumed on the 29th, climbing more than 14% in early trading, following its announcement of a plan to acquire a 50% stake in FAW Toyota through an A-share issuance — underscoring strong market interest in this state-owned automaker asset consolidation.

GAC Group announced on the evening of the 28th that it had entered into an acquisition agreement with FAW Co., conditionally agreeing to acquire the 50% stake in FAW Toyota held by FAW Co. The consideration will be paid through the issuance of A-shares at CNY 5.75 (approximately $0.86) per share. Upon completion of the transaction, FAW Toyota will be held 50-50 by GAC Group and Toyota Motor, with FAW Co. no longer holding any equity.

As of early trading on the 29th, GAC Group's Hong Kong-listed shares traded at HK$2.63 (approximately $0.34), up 4.54%, with turnover of HK$52.391 million (approximately $6.7 million). Intraday gains at one point exceeded 14%, signaling strong investor enthusiasm for the deal's prospects.

According to the announcement, in addition to issuing shares to acquire the assets, GAC Group also plans to raise supporting funds through a private placement of A-shares to no more than 35 independent third-party designated subscribers. The total amount raised is expected not to exceed the acquisition consideration, and the number of A-shares issued will not exceed 30% of the total issued share capital prior to the issuance.

Upon completion, FAW Co. will become the second-largest shareholder of GAC Group, but the transaction will not result in a change of actual controller, nor will it constitute a backdoor listing. GAC Group stated that FAW Toyota's financials will not be consolidated into the group's financial statements, but will instead be accounted for as a significant jointly controlled entity.

Notably, GAC Group's A-shares listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601238.SS) also resumed trading on the 29th. The major asset restructuring plan disclosed by the company on the 28th shows that the valuation of the target assets and the transaction price have yet to be determined.

5 Best Electric Vehicle ETFs for 2026 and How to Invest
sum: Electric vehicle (EV) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are investment funds that provide broad exposure to the EV sector. EVs are reshaping the auto industry and creating opportunities not just for automakers but also for battery makers, chip suppliers, software firms, and raw-material producers.

Picking individual winners in a fast-moving industry can be tough. That’s why many investors prefer EV-focused ETFs, which provide exposure to the trend without relying on a single company to drive returns. However, it's worth being up front about something: EV ETFs are a small segment of the market, and several options have less than $100 million in assets, where trading manipulation and closure are real risk factors you shouldn't dismiss.
With that aside, here are some of the top EV ETFs to consider.
There are several types of EV ETFs based on their investment strategy and focus area:
- Broad-based EV ETFs: These funds broadly cover the entire EV megatrend.
- Battery technology ETFs: These funds focus on companies that produce EV batteries and related materials such as lithium and cobalt.
- Autonomous vehicle ETFs: These funds focus on smart mobility and autonomous technology.

items.t: Toyota Stock: 345 Billion Currency Boost Faces Strongest Yen in Seven Months
sum: Toyota Motor TM, the world's largest automaker by vehicle sales, ran into a fresh currency headwind Monday as the yen reached its strongest level in seven months. The U.S.-listed shares were priced at $197.11, while Toyota's Tokyo stock gained 0.49% and trailed the Nikkei 225's powerful 2.1% rally. With the dollar sliding to 154.05, the foreign-exchange tailwind behind Toyota's earnings just lost more force.

Toyota's first-quarter results exposed how much that currency swing matters. Revenue climbed 10.4% to 13.53 trillion, yet operating income dropped 8.8% to 1.06 trillion. Foreign-exchange movements contributed 345 billionequal to nearly one-third of operating profitbefore management lifted its full-year revenue target to 54 trillion using an assumed rate of 160 per dollar.

The market is now roughly 3.7% stronger than Toyota's planning assumption, shrinking the currency cushion inside that upgraded forecast. Hybrid demand and aggressive cost controls still provide real protection, but a stubbornly strong yen could keep squeezing translated profits. The valuation offers some breathing room: the $197.11 share price stands 5.02% below the GF Value estimate of $207.53, suggesting modest upsidebut not enough to make the currency risk disappear.

Toyota's hybrid RAV4 is in demand as dealers wait for more supply
sum: Toyota Motor has a rare problem for an automaker: There is so much demand for its new RAV4 and the inventory is so limited that dealers only have a few days' supply.

"It is really unusual to see cars fly off the dealers' lots like this," said Jessica Caldwell, head of product insight at Edmunds. "It is not something that exists in that very practical, very suburban, small-midsize crossover segment."
At Colonial Toyota in Milford, Connecticut, the lack of RAV4s has left owner Bobby Crabtree with several open spots for new vehicles at his dealership.
"This lot can handle another 250 vehicles, so I am probably about a third full of that capacity," Crabtree said as he looked out at scores of new and used Toyotas.
Not all of those open spaces would be filled with new RAV4s during normal times, but there certainly would be more, he said.

Toyota's RAV4 has been a red-hot model over the past several years, with almost 480,000 sold in the U.S. last year. It was the third best-selling model in the country in 2025 behind the Ford F-150 and Chevrolet Silverado, two full-size pickups that have been top sellers for years, according to Cox Automotive.

When Toyota announced it would be rolling out new versions of the RAV4, two things stood out. First, the crossover utility vehicle would only be sold as a hybrid. Second, production would be limited at first and then steadily increase. In other words, there would not be the normal allotment of new RAV4s at dealerships.

Toyota Motor Corp (TM) vs Toyof: Key Differences in Stock Performance and Market Positioning
sum: Investors evaluating Toyota Motor Corp (TM) versus its OTC-traded counterpart Toyof face a choice that extends far beyond ticker symbols. The decision involves fundamental differences in liquidity, transparency, accessibility, and market positioning that directly impact execution quality, dividend reporting, and long-term portfolio outcomes. As of 2026-08-20, TM trades on the NYSE with institutional-grade liquidity and regulatory oversight, while Toyof operates in the over-the-counter market with limited transparency and broker access. This structural gap creates performance divergence that matters more than most retail investors recognize when building exposure to Toyota Motor Corporation.

Key Takeaway: TM offers superior liquidity, transparent dividend reporting, and institutional-grade execution on the NYSE, while Toyof trades OTC with limited broker access and lower transparency. Retail investors seeking Toyota exposure should prioritize TM unless specific international portfolio requirements justify the accessibility trade-offs and execution risks inherent in OTC markets. The listing venue directly determines execution quality, cost efficiency, and portfolio management flexibility.

The fundamental distinction between TM and Toyof lies in their listing venues and the cascading effects this creates across liquidity, accessibility, and valuation transparency. Both securities represent ownership in Toyota Motor Corporation, but the market infrastructure supporting each ticker produces meaningfully different investor experiences.

TM has demonstrated more stable price discovery and lower bid-ask spreads due to NYSE listing requirements and continuous institutional participation. Historical volatility patterns show TM responds more efficiently to earnings releases, production updates, and macroeconomic shifts because of concentrated liquidity and transparent order flow. According to NYSE market data, exchange-listed securities benefit from continuous price discovery mechanisms that reduce information asymmetry.

Toyof, trading over-the-counter, exhibits wider intraday spreads and delayed price adjustments to corporate events. OTC markets lack the continuous auction mechanism and regulatory transparency requirements that characterize exchange-listed securities.

Toyota Motor Corp Stock (TM) Moved Up by 3.11% on Jul 6: A Full Analysis
sum: Toyota Motor Corp (TM) moved up by 3.11%. The Automobiles & Auto Parts sector is up by 4.25%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Tesla Inc (TSLA) up 5.31%; Ford Motor Co (F) up 3.41%; Rivian Automotive Inc (RIVN) up 5.32%.

Toyota Motor Corporation (TM) experienced positive trading momentum, closing higher amid significant intraday volatility. This upward movement is primarily driven by strong U.S. sales data and a highly favorable outlook on the company's product mix, which has cushioned the impact of broader macroeconomic concerns.

The primary catalyst for the positive performance is the newly released June and second-quarter U.S. sales figures from Toyota Motor North America. The automaker reported a solid year-over-year increase in June sales, heavily supported by an exceptional surge in electrified vehicle volume, which rose double-digits. This volume growth reflects the market's ongoing appetite for hybrid models. Because hybrids command higher margins and require fewer consumer incentives than pure battery-electric vehicles, Toyota’s product strategy is yielding strong profitability, helping the stock capture a valuation premium over competitors struggling with electric-vehicle adoption.

Furthermore, investor sentiment has been bolstered by favorable long-term valuation models. In particular, several institutional and discounted cash flow models have pointed to the stock being fundamentally undervalued relative to its earnings-based intrinsic value. The company’s robust balance sheet, active share buyback initiatives, and a commitment to consistently rising dividend yields have reinforced its status as a highly stable defensive asset.

Despite these positive drivers, the stock is experiencing high volatility as investors balance the strong sales performance against known headwinds. The broader automotive sector faces ongoing pressures from international trade policies and steep tariff expenses, which have previously compressed Toyota’s net income. Additionally, upcoming executive leadership transitions scheduled for mid-July have introduced a minor layer of uncertainty regarding short-term operational shifts.

The Toyota-Joby Deal Isn't About Flying Cars — It's About Who Can Actually Build Them
sum: Ask anyone building an electric air taxi what actually keeps their program grounded, and the honest answer rarely involves rotors, batteries, or flight software. It's the assembly line.
Building One Aircraft Is Easy. Building Ten Thousand Is the Real Test

Aerospace companies have plenty of experience building a handful of incredible aircraft by hand. What almost none of them have done is build thousands of identical units consistently, safely, and cheaply enough that a ride actually pencils out financially.

That gap is the real story behind the joint venture Joby Aviation just formed with Toyota Motor Corporation, even though the official language is dressed up in talk of bringing air mobility to everyone. Building one exceptional aircraft proves an engineering team is brilliant. Building the ten-thousandth identical one proves a factory is.

Toyota has quietly backed Joby for close to a decade, contributing hundreds of millions of dollars across multiple funding rounds while loaning engineers to help with everything from seat design to production tooling. What changed this week isn't the size of the relationship — it's the shape of it.

Instead of acting as a financial backer watching from the sidelines, Toyota is now co-owner of a joint venture created specifically to industrialize Joby's aircraft. That's a fundamentally different bet. Toyota isn't just funding a flying taxi; it's putting the manufacturing system that spent decades perfecting Camrys, Corollas, and Tundras directly onto Joby's factory floor.
